summary: This is the MathWorks Navigation Toolbox documentation page for the controllerTEB step function, which computes linear and angular velocity commands and an optimized path for a robot's current pose and velocity using the Timed Elastic Band (TEB) algorithm. It documents the syntax, input and output arguments (including the extraInfo fields and ExitFlag codes 0 to 5), and version history (introduced in R2023a, ExitFlag added in R2023b). The page includes an example that plans a route with RRT* in a parking lot occupancy map and then tracks it with controllerTEB in a simulation loop. Website navigation and boilerplate are ignored.
one_line: MATLAB Navigation Toolbox documentation for the controllerTEB step function, which computes velocity commands and optimal trajectories using the Timed Elastic Band algorithm.
key_facts: The controllerTEB step function computes linear and angular velocity commands, timestamps, and an optimized path for the specified current pose and velocity of a robot.
The step function syntax is [velcmds,timestamps,optPath] = step(controller,curState,curVel), with an optional extraInfo output.
The step function was introduced in R2023a.
In R2023b, the extraInfo output argument was updated to return an additional field, ExitFlag, that specifies more information about the velocity commands, timestamps, and path.
The curState input is a three-element vector of the form [x y theta], with position in meters and orientation in radians.
The curVel input is a two-element vector of the form [v w], with linear velocity in meters per second and angular velocity in radians per second.
The velcmds output is an N-by-2 matrix whose first column is linear velocity in meters per second and second column is angular velocity in radians per second.
ExitFlag value 0 indicates that the step function returned feasible velocity commands and trajectory.
ExitFlag value 5 indicates that the robot will not reach the reference path within a specified look-ahead time even if it travels at a maximum linear velocity from its current position.
The example sets the occupancyMap resolution to 3 cells per meter for a parking lot map.
The example's RRT* planner uses MaxConnectionDistance of 0.2, with start state [2 9 0] and goal state [27 18 -pi/2].
In the example, the controllerTEB LookAheadTime is set to 10 seconds and ObstacleSafetyMargin to 0.4 meters.
In the example, the CostWeights.Time property is set to 100 to generate time-optimal trajectories.
The example's simulation loop runs while the goal is not reached and simtime is below 200 seconds, with a timestep of 0.1 seconds.
